objective: Knowledge about what an order is worth and whether it counts is spread over three modules: `pricing.py` multiplies quantities and prices, while `orders.py` and `report.py` each compare the status with the text `cancelled` on their own and import `pricing` only to add up subtotals. Move that knowledge onto the records in `stockroom/models.py` and make the other modules ask the records. Add the read-only properties `OrderLine.total_cents`, `Order.subtotal_cents` and `Order.is_active` and use them as listed in the acceptance statements. This is a pure refactor: reports and prices come out exactly as before, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `OrderLine.total_cents` is quantity times unit price in cents; `Order.subtotal_cents` is the sum of the `total_cents` of its lines (0 for an order without lines); `Order.is_active` is False for the status `cancelled` and True for `open`, `paid` and `shipped`
The three new members are properties, not dataclass fields: the field names of `OrderLine` and `Order` stay as they are, and equality and `repr` of the records are unchanged

`pricing.line_total(line)` returns `line.total_cents` and `pricing.order_subtotal(order)` returns `order.subtotal_cents`, asking the object so that a subclass overriding the property is honoured; `pricing.order_total` builds on them with the same results as before

`OrderBook.revenue_by_month`, `report.customer_totals` and `report.sales_summary` decide which orders count by asking `order.is_active` (the `N cancelled` figure of the summary is the number of orders that are not active, whatever their status text)
The same three functions take an order's amount from `order.subtotal_cents`, so an order type that overrides the property is honoured
Outside `stockroom/models.py`, no module of the `stockroom` package contains the string literal `"cancelled"` as a value of its own
`stockroom/orders.py` and `stockroom/report.py` no longer import anything from the pricing module

Output is unchanged: for the same orders, `revenue_by_month`, `customer_totals`, `sales_summary` (byte for byte), `order_total` (with and without discount and tax) and `Order.quantity` return exactly what they returned before the change
